arxiv-2011-12136.title: Introducing Sub-Riemannian and sub-Finsler Billiards Thanks: The second author would like to thank Aaron Gootjes-Dreesbach for providing comments on the first version of the paper. The first author is supported by Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG) under Germany’s Excellence Strategy EXC-2181/1 -
arxiv-2011-12136.creator: Lucas Dahinden, Álvaro del Pino
arxiv-2011-12136.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Lucas Dahinden, Álvaro del Pino. We define billiards in the context of sub-Finsler Geometry. We provide symplectic and variational (or rather, control theoretical) descriptions of the problem and show that they coincide. We then discuss several phenomena in this setting, including the failure of the reflection law to be well-defined at singular points of the boundary distribution, the appearance of gliding and creeping orbits, and the behavior of reflections at wavefronts.

arxiv-2102-06648.title: A Critical Look at the Consistency of Causal Estimation with Deep Latent Variable Models
arxiv-2102-06648.creator: Severi Rissanen, Pekka Marttinen
arxiv-2102-06648.description: Abstract Using deep latent variable models in causal inference has attracted considerable interest recently, but an essential open question is their ability to yield consistent causal estimates. While they have demonstrated promising results and theory exists on some simple model formulations, we also know that causal effects are not even identifiable in general with latent variables.

arxiv-2205-01014.description: Abstract In this paper we study intra-host viral adaptation by antigenic cooperation - a mechanism of immune escape that serves as an alternative to the standard mechanism of escape by continuous genomic diversification and allows to explain a number of experimental observations associated with the establishment of chronic infections by highly mutable viruses.

arxiv-2208-05752.title: On solutions of the Diophantine equation 𝒫 m − L n = c \mathcal{P}_{m}-L_{n}=c
arxiv-2208-05752.creator: Pagdame TIEBEKABE, Serge ADONSOU & \& Ismaïla DIOUF
arxiv-2208-05752.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Pagdame TIEBEKABE, Serge ADONSOU & \& Ismaïla DIOUF. Résumé In this article, we determine all the integers c c having at least two representations as difference between two linear recurrent sequences. This is a variant of the Pillai’s equation. This equation is an exponential Diophantine equation. The proof of our main theorem uses lower bounds for linear forms of logarithms, properties of continued fractions, and a version of the Baker-Davenport reduction method in Diophantine approximation.

arxiv-2512-09798.title: High-Resolution Water Sampling via a Solar-Powered Autonomous Surface Vehicle
arxiv-2512-09798.creator: Misael Mamani, Mariel Fernandez, Grace Luna, Steffani Limachi ∗, Leonel Apaza ∗, Carolina Montes-Dávalos, Marcelo Herrera, Edwin Salcedo
arxiv-2512-09798.description: Abstract Accurate water quality assessment requires spatially resolved sampling, yet most unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) can collect only a limited number of samples or rely on single-point sensors with poor representativeness. This work presents a solar-powered, fully autonomous USV featuring a novel syringe-based sampling architecture capable of acquiring 72 discrete, contamination-minimized water samples per mission.

arxiv-2601-02648.title: Prioritized Replay for RL Post-training
arxiv-2601-02648.creator: Mehdi Fatemi
arxiv-2601-02648.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Mehdi Fatemi. We introduce a problem-level prioritization framework for RL post-training of large language models. Building on insights from prioritized replay in deep RL, as well as prior observations that rollouts with intermediate success rates tend to produce stronger learning signals under methods such as GRPO, our approach selects problems according to a simple, model-driven priority score derived from empirical success statistics.

pmc-11664680.title: Association of Tarsometarsal Joint Slippage Following Minimally Invasive Bunionectomy with Removal of Hardware
pmc-11664680.creator: Seif El Masry, Grace DiGiovanni, Brittany M. Ammerman, Allison L. Boden, Joseph T. Nguyen, Joaquin Palma, A. Holly Johnson
pmc-11664680.description: Category:Bunion; Midfoot/ForefootIntroduction/Purpose:Following Minimally Invasive Bunionectomy (MISB), removal of hardware rates are about 5% and commonly due to midfoot pain near the distal metatarsal screw site. This distal screw head site corresponds to the proximal midshaft width measurement location, which has shown to increase postoperatively.

pmc-12522550.title: Effect of gaze direction recognition task on pain, rom and functional activities in cervicogenic headache patients
pmc-12522550.creator: Mohamed Abdelaziz Emam, Salma Ragab, András Attila Horváth, Olfat Ibrahim Ali, Zizi M. Ibrahim, Magda Ramadan
pmc-12522550.description: BackgroundCervicogenic headache is characterized by unilateral headache potentially stemming from cervical spine mechanical dysfunction. Research indicates that proprioceptive exercises, specifically gaze direction recognition (GDR), are found to be effective in reducing cervical joint position error and enhancing the quality of cervical afferent signals to the central nervous system.

pmc-12538575.title: Illuminating the druggability of the Giardia duodenalis kinome through reannotation and high-throughput screens
pmc-12538575.creator: Alexander Y.F. Lam, Isabelle S. Lucet, Aaron R. Jex, Samantha J. Emery-Corbin
pmc-12538575.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Giardia duodenalis (syn Giardia intestinalis, Giardia lamblia) is a neglected, microaerophilic gastrointestinal parasite reliant on broad spectrum anti-microaerophilic/-anaerobic nitroheterocyclic antibiotics (metronidazole) which have been in use for over 70 years. New drugs which avoid their predecessor’s shortfalls of toxic and adverse effects, as well as circumvent its increasing treatment failure, are urgently required to lower global rates of up to 200 million symptomatic cases annually. Kinases are essential regulatory enzymes that primarily catalyse the phosphorylation post-translational modification involved in dynamic cellular processes.

pmc-12603785.title: Identification of Outer Membrane Vesicles as a New Vehicle Mediating Antibiotic Resistance Gene Transfer in Campylobacter
pmc-12603785.creator: Mengyu Zhao, Min He, Xiaolong Lin, Ke Wu, Fang Yang, Xinggui Chen, Haozheng Li, Hongning Wang, Yizhi Tang
pmc-12603785.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The emergence and worldwide dissemination of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) compromise antibiotic therapy and are a major public health crisis. Horizontal gene transfer (HGT) plays a major role in the spread of ARGs among bacterial pathogens. Outer membrane vesicles (OMVs), which are membrane‐bound particles and naturally released by Gram‐negative bacteria, have been reported to carry a variety of cargos such as DNA, proteins and lipids.

pmc-12809679.title: A single-sEV analysis identifies plasma EPCAM+ sEVs as a biomarker for early diagnosis and monitoring postoperative remission of thyroid cancer
pmc-12809679.creator: Simin Yu, Yuting Luo, Tianfeng Dang, Congli Peng, Qing Gan, Yuxuan Liang, Jieqing Yu, Ping Long, Wensheng Zhou, Daofeng Dai
pmc-12809679.description: Aim: Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) are promising noninvasive biomarkers for several malignancies, including thyroid carcinoma (TC). However, their heterogeneity is frequently overlooked in bulk-level analyses. Methods: Plasma samples from TC and healthy controls (HC) were collected for a proximity-dependent barcoding assay (PBA) to identify plasma sEV biomarkers at the single-sEV level.

pmc-12978751.title: Post-Transplant Relapse in Acute Leukemia: Comparative Value of MRD and Chimerism
pmc-12978751.creator: Sinem Başak Tan Öksüz, Güldane Cengiz Seval, Klara Dalva, Selami Koçak Toprak
pmc-12978751.description: BackgroundRelapse remains the principal cause of treatment failure after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (AHSCT) in acute leukemia. Post-transplant surveillance commonly relies on measurable residual disease (MRD) and donor chimerism monitoring; however, their relative predictive value and optimal timing remain uncertain.

pmc-13222864.title: Honey yield prediction and neonicotinoid risk assessment utilizing a machine learning framework in smart agriculture
pmc-13222864.creator: Attia Ghafoor, Muhammad Majid, Hina Jahangir, Syed Ali Jafar Zaidi, Syed Rizwan Hassan, Waleed M. Ismael, Ateeq Ur Rehman
pmc-13222864.description: Reduction in pollinator abundance (predominantly honeybees) stemming from environmental and chemical stressors notably neonicotinoid pesticides poses serious threats to biodiversity and agricultural productivity. This study presents a scalable machine learning framework to foresee honey yield and assess the impact of neonicotinoid exposure.

pmc-13314703.title: Novel patient-derived tongue squamous cell carcinoma cell lines from non-smokers: 3D and in vivo models for drug response studies
pmc-13314703.creator: Graziella Ribeiro de Sousa, Guilherme da Silva Carvalho, Bruna Miyoko Ikenaga de Brito, Gabriel da Silva, Maria Clara Rezende Barbosa Lopes, Pablo Shimaoka Chagas, Elvis Terci Valera, Graziela Vieira Cavalcanti, Luiz Carlos Conti de Freitas, Andréia Machado Leopoldino
pmc-13314703.description: Tongue squamous cell carcinoma (TSCC) is the most prevalent and aggressive subtype of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), with a high incidence of lymph node metastasis even in early stages. The five-year overall survival rates remain low, around 50% in advanced stages. Cell line models are essential tools to understand the complexity of TSCC and develop new therapies.

pmc-13447799.title: Crossing the Line: Factors Associated With Escalating Pornography Use
pmc-13447799.creator: Melissa S de Roos, Laura Willkomm
pmc-13447799.description: Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM) offending has increased in recent years. Rather than being predominantly driven by an increase in associated sexual interest in children, this may be understood as a pattern of content escalation, from mainstream to extreme or even illegal pornography.

pmc-13474924.creator: Helena Přibylová, Metin Pekagirbas, Suha K. Arserim, Kardelen Yetismis, Umut Berberoglu, Unal Altug, Shirly Elbaz, Yaarit Nachum‑Biala, Oscar David Kirstein, Gad Baneth, Yusuf Özbel, Seray Töz, Carla Maia, Petr Volf, Iva Kolářová
pmc-13474924.description: BackgroundSand flies are vectors of various pathogens, primarily Leishmania and phleboviruses. The effectiveness of disease control strategies can be assessed using serological tests that measures antibodies against sand fly saliva as a marker of host exposure and a proxy biomarker of sand fly-borne pathogens transmission.
